Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to this presentation of Castellum's Q1 Report. There will be a Q and A session in the end of the webcast. If you'd like to ask a question by phone, please dial pound key five on the telephone keypad and ask your question. Let's start. Please go ahead, Pål.
Pål Ahlsén
President and CEO, Castellum
Good morning. As you probably all know by now, our main target in Castellum is to achieve a return on equity of 10% over the business cycle. During the autumn, we launched a new strategy, one could say, which we called Back to Basics. One of the main principles in Back to Basics is to increase the transaction base. During the quarter, we conducted two transactions, one smaller in Linköping, and one bigger with the disposal of nine properties to AP7, with a profit of SEK 750 million. Another principle in Back to Basics is to be very prudent with the capital that the shareholders have given us.
If we can earn it, we will return it. During the quarter we have repurchased almost 24 million shares. Another principle of Back to Basics is to have a tight grip on costs. During the autumn, we sold our co-working operation called United Spaces. We have made a reorganization and cost cuts at the headquarters, and the administrative costs, both in property management and in central administration, is lower this quarter compared to Q1 one year ago. It's almost SEK 100 million lower. Of course, leasing is also one of the main principles in Back to Basics.
It's still slow, but we have positive net leasing during the quarter, SEK 82 million, whereof SEK 72 million was the leasing to Ericsson in Hagastaden. Still slow, but positive. Castellum, our property portfolio valued to SEK 138 billion, but we also have two joint ventures. One joint venture in Gothenburg, Halvorsäng. It's logistics together with the harbor in Gothenburg. We own 37% of the shares of the listed Norwegian office company, Entra.
We have a mixed-use portfolio, mainly with office, but also a large proportion of warehouse, light industry, and public sector properties, 5.3 millionsq m lettable area, and a high sustainability focus. Now down to the details. I'll hand over to you, Christoffer.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
Thank you. Looking at the income and net operating income, both are down by some 3% compared with Q1 last year. It is mainly due to higher vacancies, but also higher direct property costs. However, with lower central administration, SEK 24 million this quarter, SEK 66 million last quarter. In addition to that, somewhat lower interest costs, some SEK 10 million, and a better contribution from Entra of SEK 17 million, it at least leaves us at positive territory in terms of income from property management. Property values were SEK +416 million or 0.3%.
As Paul mentioned, the net leasing for the period is SEK 82 million, where the large leasing in Hagastaden to Ericsson is most of that. Occupancy now at 88.0%, somewhat lower than the last quarter. On the investment side, we have net investments in the quarter of SEK 679 million. Of this, SEK 886 million investment in existing properties.
Then we sold properties for SEK 214 million, so not including the large [Inaudible], but this was transactions we made and communicated in the end of last year. The biggest one in Örebro. Into more details, income in the like-for-like portfolio decreased by SEK 47 million, and that corresponds with 2%. That is mainly due to the higher vacancies of SEK 60 million compared to the quarter last year. Both income and costs are affected by this divestment of our co-working business. This is the first full quarter without that business.
Income decreased by some SEK 45 million, and cost decreased by some SEK 63 million. That is a quarterly net SEK +8 million effect, in line with what we announced in October when we sold the company that we indicated a positive yearly effect of SEK +30 million. That's quite spot on.
On the cost side, the like-for-like property cost increased with SEK 45 million, and of this, SEK 38 million was due to higher costs for heating and snow due to the colder winter than the year before. As Pal mentioned also, looking at administration costs, and if we add both property administration and central administration, costs are down SEK 99 million. However, half of that, SEK 53 million, is related to this sold co-working business. Then please also note that we have SEK 22 million of costs that we have moved from central administration to property administration.
This is part of that change that we did in the autumn, where we both reduced costs on the headquarters, but we also moved some staff to the regions. I would also say that we in this quarter have no material one-off, which we of course have quite a lot of in Q4.
Looking at the leasing side, 14% of the total lease stocks that were up for renegotiation were renegotiated during this period with an average negative change in rent of 7.1%. It's quite a small volume. No specific or individual rental agreement behind it's actually a couple of them. As usual, the largest proportion are extended at no changes in terms. This quarter, about half of the volume, 49% or SEK 249 million is rolled over with no changes in terms.
Net leasing, as mentioned, SEK 82 million. In addition to the Ericsson deal that we have talked about, we can also mention that we have some positive net leasing in Denmark of some SEK +20 million, and we have some positive net leasing in the Mälardalen region of SEK +18 million, and that is roughly the amount of the new leasing to Life and Investor's House.
Looking at property values, as mentioned, they are up with some SEK 400 million, mainly due to the Infinity project in Hagastaden, some SEK +300 million, and also the divestment of nine properties to AP7, approximately SEK 250 million. It was also communicated in the press release in that transaction. If we take those two away, the remaining part is actually a little bit lower than the last quarter. SEK 138 billion of fair value, and this then of course includes the SEK 5.6 billion transaction with AP7, as that one is closing in Q2. Well, a small part of it is actually in Q3, but the big part in Q2.
Also in this quarter, we have actually lower cash flow expectations in our valuations, and that's the downward pressure on rental levels. That's the explanation to this smaller negative value changes if we exclude Infinity and AP7 transactions.
Looking at the financing side, market conditions remain favorable despite increased volatility. We saw some credit spreads widening during the quarter as the conflict in the Middle East escalated, but we have recovered continuously during the quarter and now in the beginning of Q2, and spreads in the bond market are some 10, 15 bps wider than the lows before the conflict started. Nordic banks continue to offer very competitive pricing and are willing to increase volumes.
It's also on this side that we have been active in the quarter on the secured side with the refinancing of in total SEK 6.8 billion in bank loans. The average duration of those loans has been just over eight years, so quite long credit duration in the bank loans that we offer currently. That is of course contributing to the increase in our average debt maturity.
We still have some SEK 18 billion in cash and unutilized credit facilities, providing us with comfortable backup to the upcoming maturities, which are not very big. Financial key ratios are broadly stable compared to previous quarter. However, slight increase in the loan-to-value, now at 37.5%, and mainly explained by the fact that we have bought shares in the quarter of some SEK 2 billion, while the proceeds from the transactions comes in Q2. ICR stable at 3.2x, and comfortable headroom against policies of 40% LTV and 3.0x ICR.
As mentioned on the previous slide, average debt maturity is now slightly higher, 4.5 years, and the average fixed interest term is three years. Interest-bearing liabilities slightly up, same explanation, a bit higher due to the mismatch in acquiring shares in the quarter and proceeds from the transactions in the next quarter. Looking at the divestments, we have done, as mentioned, one large transaction and one small transaction. The last one we have talked about quite a lot already. SEK 5.6 billion public assets.
100% leased out, sold to [Inaudible]. Fair value as of Q4 was SEK 5.16 billion. The total earnings, I think, was SEK 715 million. That one is closing now in Q2 and Q3. The smaller one, maybe not small for the Linköping market, SEK 256 million sold to the Wallenstam family. A big difference, 25% vacancies. From our perspective, quite a lot of investment needs in the portfolio going forward, and a good transaction from our perspective.
An update on the share buybacks that we are conducting. After the divestment of the portfolio to Atrium Ljungberg, the board announced that we are initiating a share buyback program in total of SEK 3.4 billion. Of that, we have so far acquired for SEK 2.7 billion. That is up until today or yesterday evening, I believe.
Out of that, some SEK 2 billion was acquired during the quarter, and then the remaining ones now in April. Average price, SEK 113 per share. A large lease during that quarter, 24,000sq m in Halmstad. The entire building with a 15-year duration. It includes an option for the tenant up until 1 June 2026. Roughly in a month, we will know if they have the optionality to decrease it to a five-year tenant with approximately half of the volume.
To wrap things up, some words on our sustainability performance. The day-to-day work to decrease our energy consumption goes on as previously, and during the quarter, we have reduced the energy consumption in the like-for-like portfolio with 4%, and roughly 1/4 of our electricity is self-generated mostly by solar panels. Before we let all the questions in, let me summarize a bit.
We have positive net leasing, SEK +82 million, whereof SEK 72 million from Ericsson. It's Q4 in a row with positive net leasing, but very low figures, one could say. It remains slow in the leasing market. We made two transactions very successfully, I would say, and that's part of the Back to Basics principle to remove everything that we don't believe will give a 10% return on equity. The cost savings program we conducted during the autumn now comes into the figures. With that, I think we can hand over to questions.
Yes, we do. So if you'd like to ask a question by phone, please dial pound key five, and ask a question. The first question comes from Tobias Chai, Nordea.
Tobias Chai
Equity Research Analyst, Nordea
Good morning. Thank you for the presentation and for taking my questions. First I have a couple of general questions. Regarding your portfolio, is it possible to, in some way, quantify how large proportion that you think that doesn't meet your return requirements?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
Not really. I think we are looking at that continuously, and one thing that's very important in that equation is actually what prices you can achieve. It's difficult to answer that question, but I would say there's a big proportion that actually can achieve 10%. There's a proportion also that I would say is borderline, and then there's a proportion that probably not, depending on prices, that not will meet our 10% return requirement. I cannot give you a figure on that right now.
Tobias Chai
Equity Research Analyst, Nordea
That's fair. Can I follow up? How does that view impact your view on projects? If you complete a project with a long lease to a stable tenant and it's fully let, is it possible to continue to own those kind of properties, or should those properties be sold as they are completed, or do you give promises to the tenant that you will remain as a long-term owner, so you can't sell it?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
The last question, that's very uncommon, that you have to promise tenants to keep something forever and ever. I wouldn't say that that's a question. If we complete something and obviously then the property is in its prime.
The demand for those type of properties may vary in different markets, depending on the market and interest rates, may be very high, but it's from case to case, I would say.
Tobias Chai
Equity Research Analyst, Nordea
Okay, thank you. Regarding your renegotiations, even though it's a small number, is it related to some specific region or some specific category?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
No, actually, no. Quite a lot of the different underlying rental agreements, and actually different categories, and different geographies. That's unfortunately not.
Tobias Chai
Equity Research Analyst, Nordea
Okay. Regarding your admin expenses, both the level of expenses for central admin in Q1 and the movement from central admin to property admin in Q1, is that a reasonable level also for coming quarters or are there some seasonal variations in those numbers?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
No seasonal variations. That's roughly in line with the expectations, although we of course not guide on it, but it's quite clean, so to say. No one-offs in it.
Tobias Chai
Equity Research Analyst, Nordea
Okay, perfect. That's all from me. Thank you.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
Thank you. The next question, Lars Norrby, SEB.
Lars Norrby
Equity Research Analyst, SEB
Good morning. Question about buybacks. By the way, I love your commentary. If we can't earn it, we will return it. You still have some way to go on the SEK 3.4 billion buyback program that you have. On top of that, I guess you have the capital distribution for 2025, a few hundred million on that one. To do even more than that, but does that necessitate more divestments of properties?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
At least we do not have any plans for more than that, should we not do any more divestments.
Lars Norrby
Equity Research Analyst, SEB
You've done some quite sizable divestments to SEK 5.9 billion and close to SEK 300 million or so, but still your total portfolio is something like SEK 138 billion. Why haven't you been able to do more? I guess you want to do much more than that. Isn't that true?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
What we see right now, I would say that we see quite a big interest in general on the property transaction market to make transactions. That's quite clear. More in detail than that, I don't think we can have some more detail than that. We have discussions with interested parties, and as soon as we have something to tell, we will definitely tell.
Lars Norrby
Equity Research Analyst, SEB
Okay. Thank you.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
Next question, Nadir Rahman, UBS.
Nadir Rahman
Real Estate Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Hello. Sorry. Can you hear me now?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
.
Nadir Rahman
Real Estate Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Sorry, I think I was muted. Apologies. Sorry, I'd already started. Yes. I have two questions from me. The first one is, in your report, if we look at the value decline in the markets that you mentioned have a lower expected cash flows, I'm assuming this is firstly not Kista, Finland, which you said you took value declines on in Q4. Could you give some more color as to where this decline was concentrated? I can ask my second question after this.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
Not really any concentration to that. You are correct that Kista, Finland was more Q4, so this is more broadly across the portfolio.
Nadir Rahman
Real Estate Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Okay. Second question is on the slight decline in rental income, and of course an opportunity as well. You're mentioning that this is largely due to the effect of a legacy, like negative net lettings from last year. When do we expect this to start to inflect and we start to see a more positive effect from any positive nettings from the last four quarters? Do you have perhaps an indication of when we see that inflection?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
We don't really have that indication. Maybe we have that indication, but we don't guide on it. What we could mention is, of course, that Q1 last year was very negative, net leasing-wise, and that this positive, very small figure, but positive Q2, Q3, and Q4, and now positive again in Q1 this year. We can't give more details than that.
Nadir Rahman
Real Estate Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Okay, very clear. Just to come back to my initial question on the value decline. Instead of any regional concentration, is there any asset class, for example, offices or any other sector that you see this value decline occurring in more?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
Not really there either. It's actually in different asset classes. I mean quite small volume in the big perspective, I would say.
Nadir Rahman
Real Estate Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Okay. Very clear. Thank you.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
Thank you. Next question from John Vuong, Kempen.
John Vuong
Director of Equity Research, Kempen
Hi, good morning. In the previous energy crisis, Castellum wasn't really fully hedged against electricity costs. With the war ongoing, could you provide a bit more color on how well you're now protected against a surge in electricity prices?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
Look, we changed that a couple of years ago to a more, maybe more normal, I don't know, but at least a different hedging strategy, more classic, 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% strategy. I would say better hedged. Not fully hedged, but better hedged and quite evenly over the couple of years.
John Vuong
Director of Equity Research, Kempen
Okay, that's clear. Thank you. Just on the share buyback, I think in your latest press release from this week, I noticed that there were no repurchases done on Friday and Monday. I suppose that also coincides with the share price above SEK 125. Could you provide a bit more color on this?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
That's correct. That was... As of lately, we have bought back shares through this safe harbor procedure, as we have been in close period, and then we instructed the bank on that share price maximum.
John Vuong
Director of Equity Research, Kempen
Okay, thank you. Just lastly, on the occupancy, I noticed you restated several numbers. Could you highlight what has changed and why it has changed?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
Could you repeat the question?
John Vuong
Director of Equity Research, Kempen
On your occupancy definition, I noticed you restated some historical numbers in the quarterly reporting. What has changed in the definition of occupancy, and why did you change it?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
What we have changed is that previously our occupancy was for the full period, where now we have changed it into end of period. The reason for that is that we think that's more accurate, especially when it comes to the end of the year, when you are very much affected by the vacancy level in the first quarters of the year. I think that's more common that the vacancy figure or occupancy figures are end of period figures.
John Vuong
Director of Equity Research, Kempen
Okay, that's clear. Thank you.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
Thank you. Next question, Paul May, Barclays.
Paul May
Director and Head of Real Estate Equity Research, Barclays
Hi, guys. Thanks for the presentation. Just a couple quick ones from me. You mentioned obviously looking at disposals and selling assets where you don't hit your return requirements. Just wondering who would be the buyers of those assets, because there's not many buyers or much capital out there that's looking for the low returns that you would anticipate on those assets and hence you're trying to sell them. Just wondering if you could give some color on that would be great.
Secondly, on the operating environment, appreciate it's not particularly been easy out there, and as you've highlighted, it's quite tough. I think you've talked about improving the leasing environment, improving the operating metrics. When should we expect those to actually flow through into real numbers in terms of occupancy and NRI growth, which seems to be getting worse rather than better? Is it to do with your weaker assets or weaker locations, or do you just think it's a market-wide soft leasing market that just requires time before that starts to improve? Thanks.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
I can start with the first question. We actually disagree a bit. We think it's plenty of interest out there, plenty of capital out there interested in very large proportion of our assets. I would say that's from different kinds of capital investors as well, local, foreign, institutional, private, listed real estate companies, private equity funds, and not least the Swedish institutions. We think it's very much interest in the transaction market.
Pål Ahlsén
President and CEO, Castellum
Regarding the operational figures, vacancy and like for like growth, I would imagine we're not guiding, but I would imagine that we will continue to see a pretty slow market for a while. We haven't seen any turnaround as of yet anyways. Until we reach sort of a new equilibrium where we are, we probably will see figures that are a bit on the downslope before it turns, and this was also, I think we indicated that during the autumn that it will get a bit worse before it can improve.
Now we at least have positive net letting. Even if it's dancing around the zero, but it's still positive. We are not seeing a rapid increase in demand for our properties in the rental market as it is.
Paul May
Director and Head of Real Estate Equity Research, Barclays
Thank you.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
Thank you.
Thanks. Next question, Pranava Boyidapu. Sorry if I'm pronouncing it wrong, also Barclays.
Pranava Boyidapu
Director of Real Estate Credit and Securitization Research, Barclays
Hello. Thank you for taking my question. I'm Paul May's credit analyst. On that note, I would like to get a little bit more clarity on what your if you can't earn it, we'll return it policy means for the bondholders. Because, again, at the cost of sounding repetitive, there are some loose ends with the consent solicitation that didn't go through specifically for the Castellum 2029 euro bonds.
Just wondering, at what point in your business plan does it seem like you could potentially consider the bondholders on the side of a cessation of business event?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
Same answer that we have said before, that if and when we come to that point in time that we are having such transactions sort of on the table, then we will handle it at that point in time.
Pranava Boyidapu
Director of Real Estate Credit and Securitization Research, Barclays
I have a second question. Regarding your hybrid debt, which is, I believe, SEK 1 billion with the first call next year, I was wondering if you had any plans in terms of how you expect to refinance it considering the size of it. I assume that the hybrids will remain a part of your capital structure. If there are potentially different currencies you might consider, or is it going to be euros?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
Also on that one, we will announce our plans sort of when we have decided on our plans.
Pranava Boyidapu
Director of Real Estate Credit and Securitization Research, Barclays
All right. Thank you very much.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO and Acting Head of Transactions, Castellum
Thank you. That seems to be the last question of today. Thank you all for listening and thanks for the questions. Yes. Thank you, and until next time.
Operator
The host has ended this call. Goodbye.

Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Castellum's Q4 report. From our side, it's myself, Christoffer Strömbäck, acting CFO, and Pål Ahlsén, CEO. There will be a Q&A session in the end of the webcast, and if you'd like to ask a question by phone, please dial pound key five on your telephone keypad and ask your question. Let's start. Please go ahead, Pål.
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
Thank you, Christoffer, and thank you to all that are phoning in. I would like to start with saying that I've been here for almost six months, and I've got a very warm welcome from all of our staff. I'm very thankful for that. Also from shareholders that have reached out with questions, challenging questions, and also very good advice. I hope that will continue going forward because that's, that's something that actually makes Castellum better, being challenged by our shareholders. I really appreciate that. The focus for us the past six months has been back to basics, the sort of the new strategy of Castellum, and the focus is crystal clear. Our target is to deliver a 10% return on equity over the business cycle. That's, that's really been what we've been working on for the past six months.
It's all about taking away things that are not relevant, that are unnecessary. It's all about leasing, decreasing our vacancy rate, increasing our occupancy rate, and it's about cost control, reducing our costs, both in administration, but also in our operations. We have also gone through our portfolio to see which properties are winners that we can keep in the long term, and properties that are struggling a bit more, where we either have to change our business plan or we actually have to leave them to someone else who has other ideas or other visions for the future than we have. That has been really the focus for the past six months, and we call that back to basics. One of the things we've done, which I mentioned, was decreasing costs.
Unfortunately, we were in a situation where we had a bit of a too, too big of a cost, which led to staff reduction, unfortunately, during the autumn, where 30 people had to leave Castellum, and that cost us around SEK 40 million during the Q4. We believe, though, that the savings will be roughly the same amount going forward due to that action. One of the key things for us is having room to maneuver when it comes to the portfolio, freedom to change the portfolio. Without that freedom or without that room to maneuver, it will practically be impossible for us to reach 10% return on equity. We had some right things or conditions in our bond agreements, which we addressed in the end of last year.
It's called cessation of business, which sort of limited our room to maneuver. We asked the bondholders if we could change those conditions, terms and conditions, and most of them agreed to that in December. That also came with a cost of roughly SEK 30 million, and that's also something that is in the Q4 report we are talking about today. Property values are down SEK 2.5 billion last year and SEK 1 billion in the Q4. The main reason for the value changes are changes of expectations of future cash flow, which is mainly due to changes in long-term vacancy and rental prices or rental levels. In the Q4, SEK 1 billion in value changes, negative value changes, with mainly Kista, half a billion.
Kista is a small proportion of our portfolio. It's well known in Sweden, I would say. It's often written about it in the newspaper, and we have roughly 130,000sq m in Kista, and it's around 2% of our portfolio, but it's struggling a bit with vacancy, and that's one of the challenges we have within our portfolio. Finland, we have also changed sort of the expected long-term vacancy, which has led to a reduction in property value of roughly SEK 200 million. Net leasing for the year was negative SEK 140 million. Most of the negative event was actually in the Q1, where net leasing was down SEK 184 million, and that was mainly two events. It was Boozt down in Malmö....
Northvolt, the bankruptcy of Northvolt. Since then, the Q2, Q3, and Q4 has actually been positive, but not as positive as the negative events of the Q1. Net leasing SEK 140 million negative. Many people obviously ask if we can see a turnaround. We obviously hope so, but our focus is leasing, leasing, leasing. Time will tell if there has been a turnaround or not. One of the things we've launched, now, actually in January, is what we call Castellum Business School. We believe that we need to raise the awareness within the company on how to understand the strategy, for example, but also to increase efficiency in the property management, in project management, and in leadership, and things related to the Castellum business. We launched the Castellum Business School in January.
All staff will get relevant education, given their occupation, but also 150 people have been selected to do the Castellum Business School MBA, including calculation, leadership, training, and so on and so forth. We believe that that will be a positive contribution to our aim to reach 10% return on equity. My final point here in the intro is the fact that the board is proposing share buybacks instead of dividend, and that's in line with our new policy for capital distribution. We think that's a, that is a wise thing to do today when the share price is where it is in relation to the net asset value. We can actually skip, go to the next slide and just give you a background on Castellum. We are listed company, obviously.
We have property value of roughly SEK 137 billion, where most of it is in major cities in Sweden, Stockholm, Gothenburg, and Malmö. We also have a strong presence in regional cities, growing cities like Örebro, Jönköping, and Västerås. We have a portfolio also in Helsinki, Finland, roughly SEK 6 billion, and SEK 5 billion in Copenhagen. Then we have a pretty significant stake in a Norwegian company, office company, listed, where we have almost 38% of the shares. 5.3 million square meters, and a yearly contracted rent of SEK 9.3 billion and high sustainability focus. Christoffer?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Yes, thank you. Summarizing the full year 2025 and comparing it with the same period last year, it is negatively affected by mainly divestments and higher vacancies. That is shown in sort of all of the results figures on this page. In addition to that, and as Pål mentioned, negative value changes of the property is SEK 2.5 billion for the full year and SEK 1.1 billion for the Q4, -1.8% for the full year. This all summarizing gives some return on equity of 1.2%, which of course is much lower than our target of 10%.
Net leasing, Pål also mentioned -140, very negative one in the Q1, and then the three quarters after that, positive ones. In the Q4, SEK +26 million. Occupancy is fairly stable, 89.8%, roughly the same as last quarter. We have, during the year, invested quite a lot, SEK 4.4 billion, a combination of investing in our properties, is the most of it. In addition to that, we also made some acquisitions during 2025. Pål mentioned a few one-offs, we have a couple of one-offs in Q4, isolated, both positive ones and negative ones, and we will try to go through all of them during this call.
Looking at it in more detail, in the like-for-like portfolio, income increased by SEK 26 million, that is 0.3%. Index contributed with SEK 140 million, but it's done, offset by higher vacancies of SEK 190 million. Then we have one of the first one-offs, which is SEK 58 million in a one-off, relating to a reversal of accrued annuity for the Northvolt. That's a difficult one. We took the full net leasing, negative net leasing in Q1, but then now in Q4, we sort of concluded the final parts of the rental agreement with the bankruptcy estate. Then we had no cash effect, but an accrued one that we reversed during Q4. So that was a SEK +58 to 68 million in Q4.
Direct property costs, like for like, increased by SEK 68 million, corresponding to 2.7%. We have a mild winter. Now we're talking Q4, not what we have seen after Q4, but in Q4, a mild winter. The cost for heating and snow removal was actually decreased year compared to last year. Then we have, you know, that was offset by some higher rent losses. We also, during Q4, isolated, took a couple of larger wasted projects or projects, projects that we are not expecting to go through anymore. Yeah, so one-offs of that one recorded under maintenance in Q4.
Central administration and property administration in total increased by SEK 54 million, and here we have another one-off. Pål mentioned it, approximately SEK 40 million of those SEK 64 million is one-off relating to the staff reduction on head office reorganization. We can go to the next slide, please. Looking at the leasing renegotiations of SEK 279 million, that is 11% of the total lease stock up for renegotiation. Fairly the same rent as before, decrease of 0.1%, so very flat. That's quite low volume of the total stock up for renegotiation. The very large bulk of it, 62% for SEK 1.6 billion is actually, yeah, just prolonged. Prolonged at the same terms as before.
Yeah, that is something I think is very much worth mentioning. Net leasing, we have been talking about already, and here we also have the figures in the graph up to the right showing that, as mentioned, the very big part of it was a -1 in Q1, but a very big part of that was the Northvolt bankruptcy. Then we have three positive quarters, not big figures, of course, but at least positive. Property values, we have been through most of the figures already, actually. SEK 1.1 billion down in Q4. Stockholm stands for 0.9 of that, and Finland, 0.2.
As Pål mentioned, of the Stockholm, SEK 0.9 billion down, SEK 0.5 billion is related to Kista. Valuation yield, fairly flat, 1 basis point up from last quarter, but, you know, 5.64%. Fairly stable as well. I think we take the next slide up. Looking at the financial highlights and our funding situation, overall, the funding markets where we are present, i.e., the banking market, the SEK bond market, the euro bond market, as well as the hybrid markets are all very favorable at the moment, I would say. Very good market conditions for net margins at good levels, yeah, very much liquidity in all of the markets.
Current spread in the domestic or the SEK market is some 80 basis points for three-year money, some 110, 150 for five-year money. Banks offer us typically five-year money, 110 to 130 basis points, also at good levels, good volumes. I would say that most of them or maybe all of them would like to increase their positions, but that's very good. During Q4, isolated, we did not actually do that many funding actions. We made one bond, SEK 1 billion, 122 basis points, 5.25 years. Bought back some bonds at the same time. Then as Pål mentioned earlier, we made this consent solicitation. Overall, we got the results that we were expecting, so that's good.
Average interest rate 3.1, stable compared to last year, actually down a little bit since the year before. We see potential for actually reducing this a little bit going forward. Also on the financing side, we have a couple of one-offs. Together, they are approximately SEK 50 million. As Pål mentioned, 30 of them are connected to this consent solicitation, and then we have an additional approximately SEK 20 million for refinancing and early redemption, both coupled to loans and to bonds. Quite large one-offs in the financial items as well. On this slide, we have our financial key ratios. Very stable, I would say. Small changes compared to last quarter. Loan-to-value, 36.5%. ICR, 3.2. Good headroom to our policy.
We have LTV policy of 40%, ICR policy of 3x. Good headroom there. At the beginning of this year, S&P confirmed our BBB flat with stable outlook. That's about what has happened on the rating side. Debt maturities still stable, 4.3 years. We are quite happy with our funding situation and our key ratios ability. I hand over to you, Pål.
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
Yeah, one of the things which we are very good at, I would say, in within Castellum, it's the reduction of energy consumption within our properties. Last year, we actually reduced the energy consumption in our portfolio with almost 7%. That's one of the things I really like about Castellum, is this key focus on reducing costs for energy, but then also from a sustainability perspective. That's something to be very proud of. 58% of our portfolio is sustainability certified, and we actually have 24% of our electricity self-generated. High level of sustainability within Castellum, something to be proud of.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Super! If you'd like to ask a question by phone, please dial pound key five on the telephone keypad and ask your question. The first question comes from Jan Ihrfelt at Kepler Cheuvreux.
Jan Ihrfelt
Financial Analyst, Kepler
Okay. Good morning. Thanks for taking my questions. Actually, I have four of them. I start with the sentiment on the rental market, office market. Have you seen any change in Q1 compared to Q4?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
Reluctant to speculate, and it's very early actually in the quarter to say anything about that. When I speak with the staff in the offices, I can say they still say that it's a challenging market. Our only focus is to do whatever we can to reduce vacancy.
Jan Ihrfelt
Financial Analyst, Kepler
Okay. The next question, you had a net letting figure for the full year of SEK -140 million. I'm just little bit asking about the overhang into 2026. How much of this SEK 140 million has already hit the P&L?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
We actually don't have a specific figure on that one. I mean, typically, there is a lag, as you know. You know, and in this case, it's very much so. We got a big portion, as you know, in Q1 was in North America, and they have actually made run for the full year, 2025. Not all of the volume, but quite a lot of it. That is coming in with full effect, 2026. We don't have a-
Jan Ihrfelt
Financial Analyst, Kepler
Okay.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Figure to give on that.
Jan Ihrfelt
Financial Analyst, Kepler
No, no, exactly. Okay. Bringing down vacancies, you know, how 10%, and, I'm just looking at some kind of a timeframe here. When, at what time, point in time would you get down to 5%? Have you any timeframe there?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
That's an impossible question to answer, and it's... We are not doing that type of forecast. As I think I mentioned that in the Q3 report, that we know that it will probably be a bit worse before it becomes better, in relating to your previous question. We are not making any forecasts when it comes to vacancy ratios.
Jan Ihrfelt
Financial Analyst, Kepler
My last question regards the one-off, the SEK 40 million, and where is it recorded? Is it all in central administration, or is it split to some other lines?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
It's a split between central administration and property administration.
Jan Ihrfelt
Financial Analyst, Kepler
Yeah, and the ratio between them?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
I don't have that ratio, actually. I can come back on that.
Jan Ihrfelt
Financial Analyst, Kepler
Okay. Thanks for taking my questions.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Thank you. The next question, Lars Norrby, SEB.
Lars Norrby
Equity Research Analyst, SEB
Well, thank you, and good morning. Part of your back to basic strategy is to, I quote, "Divest non-core assets." Far, since you assumed the role as CEO, Pål, you haven't done that much. I think there was some SEK 300 million completed in Q4, and you announced through a press release, an additional SEK 500 million, which in the context of a portfolio of SEK 137 billion, is not that much. Then you also mentioned that you made some changes to your bond terms in the Q4. My first question is, is there anything now holding you back from finding significant divestments?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
No, I wouldn't say so. The transaction market is quite vivid, I would say. Christoffer mentioned that the market for lending money is very favorable right now, so it's a huge interest, actually, in making transactions in the property world. We see we have lots of discussion, people reaching out to see to find a deal. Nowadays, if I may, reminisce of how it was 30 years ago, transactions went much faster than they do today. The due diligence phase in making transactions are so much more due diligent, so to say. Even if I wish that we had a higher pace, that's not how the business works, nowadays. I can assure you that we are doing everything we can to, high, to reach this target of high, of a high transaction.
Lars Norrby
Equity Research Analyst, SEB
Okay, and my second and final question is: What is a non-core asset in your portfolio?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
To be quite honest, I don't think I've never, ever used the word core or non-core, so I never said that. Our core assets are the ones we have, I would say. Some of them are perhaps giving a too low rate of return, given our expectations of the future. Our core assets are actually commercial real estate in Sweden. It might be hotels, it might be offices, it might be logistics or light warehouses, and so on and so forth. I never actually use the words core or non-core. We are more, let's say, looking at what we believe that they can give us in return going forward, and those who are helping us in reaching our targets, that's our core assets. That's not office, that's not that, that's not this. That's how we're thinking about that.
Lars Norrby
Equity Research Analyst, SEB
Okay, thank you.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Thank you, Lars. Next question from Nadir at UBS.
Nadir Rahman
Real Estate Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Hi, good morning. Can you hear me clearly?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Yes. Yes.
Nadir Rahman
Real Estate Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Wonderful. Thank you both for taking my questions. I've got a few, and I'll ask them one by one, if that's okay. Firstly, you're saying on your capital distribution, you are now allocating your full distribution to buybacks rather than dividends. I think, Pål, you mentioned, quote, unquote, "simple mathematics" in your presentation. If there is simple ways to split it, then is your thinking that if you're trading at a discount, you then do buybacks, and if you're trading at a premium or closer to that, you're doing dividends? Or is there a more, is there a more nuanced way that you're looking at the this distribution policy going forward, it isn't really that simple?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
I would say it's really that simple, even if you can make it a bit more complicated. Now, the discount is quite big, right? It's 32, 33%, and then you don't have to think about it that much. Once, and hopefully when that gap closes, we have to have a deeper discussion when it's time to switch to dividend from share buyback.
Nadir Rahman
Real Estate Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Got it. Okay, and a quick follow-up to that as well. What is your exact execution plan on the buybacks through the year? I know it's SEK 1.2 billion, it isn't a small proportion of your market cap. How do you propose you perform the buybacks this year?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Our thinking is that we should wait until after the AGM. We think that we should adopt the financial results for 2025, i.e., the part of that results that we are distributing to our shareholders. We will wait until AGM, and we will come back with details after that.
Nadir Rahman
Real Estate Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Okay. Got it. Very clear. Thank you. My second question is, I won't be using the word core and non-core, as Pål mentioned, but looking at some pain points in the portfolio, such as Kista, Finland, where you've taken more substantial write-downs and values, and also they have elevated vacancies. What is your thinking on these regions and generally, your, your focus on trying to become more Sweden-centric? I think that's something you mentioned in your Q3 report.
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
More Sweden-centric, I wouldn't write that. I would say continue. We are already Swedish-centric, so that is not a change, I would say. Well, Kista, it's a small proportion of our portfolio. It's very well known in Sweden, that's why we highlight it. It's struggling and has been struggling for a long time. We are picking our brains, finding a way to reduce vacancy and make a turnaround in Kista. I would be quite, quite honest to say that that's not an easy nut to crack, but we are really working on that. Vacancy 22% in our portfolio, probably in Kista, perhaps more than 30%. It's a challenging market, but again, small proportion of our portfolio. Again, we are really picking our brains, trying to figure out how to make a turnaround, at least for our properties in Kista. Finland, it's also a challenging market, just as it has been in Stockholm, Gothenburg, and Malmö, and Copenhagen, and to some extent, also in Oslo. Again, we are also trying there to find ways to reduce vacancy and, keeping rent levels stable, just as we do for Kista.
Nadir Rahman
Real Estate Equity Research Analyst, UBS
That's very clear. Thank you. My third question is then moving to a different part of the Nordic region, Entra and your stake there. I think you mentioned that it's a fairly attractive market in Norway at the moment, despite the swap rates being slightly higher, and inflation is more elevated relative to, let's say, Sweden and Finland. What is your thinking on the Entra stake, going into this year? I know there was an increase in the stake, in Q1 last year, so are there any thoughts on this?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
I really like Entra. Entra is a great, great company, and I think Castellum can probably learn quite a bit from Entra. I appreciate the cooperation we have with Entra. Obviously, it's not an optimal situation, I think, where we have the stake we have. Balder has its stake it has. It's a low free float for other shareholders. Perhaps it's not the best long-term solution. I don't have any answers to the long-term solution today, not at all. What one should say is that Entra is performing quite well, so it's not hurting us in any way, having that stake in Entra, because it's a good company. They have a nice portfolio, nice management, and so it's not something that is dragging us down, not at all. The contrary, actually.
Nadir Rahman
Real Estate Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Okay, very clear. My final question is, on your recent leasing of the Infinity building in Hagastaden. I know, there's been some talk in the press of who the tenant may be, but could you provide some more details, potentially, on the yields, the rent levels, and more generally, the discussions you've been having on letting? Are they with large tenants and public companies, or are they increasingly with smaller companies and potentially SMEs?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
Actually, we cannot elaborate at all regarding. We've sent out the information we can send out, and that's been requested from the tenant. We will disclose more when they have either used or not used the option to reduce the number of square meters they will have, and then we will provide you with more information. Obviously, we're very happy that Ericsson has selected our building, Infinity. It will be a great building, and I think Ericsson will have nice time sitting there in Hagastaden, in our building.
Nadir Rahman
Real Estate Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Okay, very clear. Just to follow up on the size of maybe the tenants that you're speaking to more generally in the markets for lettings. Are they larger tenants and companies, or do you think that the general size of those companies and
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
Uh, our-
Nadir Rahman
Real Estate Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Is there more skewed to SMEs?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
Our portfolio is, has a, is a broad palette of very different type of buildings. We just don't have office, we have other type of buildings as well. We are, are speaking to a very broad palette of Swedish businesses.
Nadir Rahman
Real Estate Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Okay. That's very clear. Thank you.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Thank you. Next question, Edoardo from Deutsche Bank.
[Analyst] (Deutsche Bank)
Analyst, Deutsche Bank
Good morning, both. Basically, I had two questions. The first one is on the consent solicitation process for your bonds. As you mentioned, you got approval from majority of your bondholders. However, there is still one particular bond, the 2029s, which actually has even more constraining language compared to the other ones, which hasn't received consent. Hence, I was wondering what you intend to do with this particular bond, because I guess the 2026, in any case, is during the very short term.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Yeah, I mean, so what we mean when we say that we have better flexibility now is, of course, that the volume outstanding that is having this language is much lower. Should we, in the future, sometime, have transactions on the table, then we will manage that at that point in time.
[Analyst] (Deutsche Bank)
Analyst, Deutsche Bank
Okay. You may, at some point, you know, revisit the content vis-à-vis this bond when you sell the assets?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Yeah, exactly. I mean, we will, we will have a look at that, at that point in time.
[Analyst] (Deutsche Bank)
Analyst, Deutsche Bank
Okay. Thank you. My second question is about the hybrid. I was wondering what and when you intend to do regarding the non-call 26?
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
I mean, we are first of all, well, that we're happy with our hybrid. It's as you know, running with a 3.125% coupon, which is of course that very good level. We are happy about that. Yeah, I mean, we like the instrument, we like the levels we have today and do not want to speculate about future actions regarding the hybrid.
[Analyst] (Deutsche Bank)
Analyst, Deutsche Bank
Okay. Thank you very much.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Thank you. The next question, Pranava from Barclays.
Pranava Boyidapu
Director of Credit Research, Barclays
Thank you for taking my question. I have a couple of follow-ups on what you just said regarding the consent solicitation. With the 26 and the 29s together, that's roughly 30% of all your bonds outstanding. Clearly that is not giving you the amount of flexibility that you suggested. If I could ask, what was driving the timing of the consent solicitation that you did last year, if you had not lined up any specific action immediately? The second question regarding your hybrid. The hybrid language, of course, doesn't have the same kind of constraints, but I was wondering if there's anything that would potentially require consent solicitation as well.
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
To the first question, back to the transaction market and the, and the transaction, it's also that transactions takes time. I, and going into transactions, you're very helpful with better visibility of our, our situation. That is probably the, the answer to the, to the first question. Now we think that we have that flexibility. We, I mean, the results were pretty spot on what we were expecting, so we are happy about that. At 26, I mean, that, that's, very close, coming up now in the September, I think it is.
Pranava Boyidapu
Director of Credit Research, Barclays
Thank you, and regarding the hybrids?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
Sorry, I didn't get. I got the question now.
Pranava Boyidapu
Director of Credit Research, Barclays
Regarding the hybrids, is there any language in there that would accelerate or impede your future, you know, change in portfolio?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
No, no language in the hybrid was. I'm aware. No.
Pranava Boyidapu
Director of Credit Research, Barclays
Okay. Thank you very much.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Thank you. Next question from John at Kempen.
John Vuong
Director of Equity Research, Kempen
Hi, good morning. Just on the net letting, are you seeing any differences between geographies and asset classes in terms of terminations as well as leasing?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
I think in general, what one can say is that the market that has been struggling in the downturn that they have been experiencing is, first of all, office and in major cities, in bigger cities. Then we have had a softer downturn in regional cities, where it has perhaps not been a downturn. Offices in major cities like Stockholm, Gothenburg, and Malmö, then in Copenhagen and Helsinki, is struggling a bit more than we can see in regional cities.
John Vuong
Director of Equity Research, Kempen
The positive turn in Q3 and Q4, is that skewed to any specific asset class or geography?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
Could you repeat the question?
John Vuong
Director of Equity Research, Kempen
That net letting turning positive in Q3 and Q4, is that driven by any specific region or specific asset class?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
No.
John Vuong
Director of Equity Research, Kempen
Clear. You mentioned that you're looking into improving the occupancy in more challenging markets. What ways are you seeing in your first look into that? Is it- can it be easily solved with, say, CapEx, or does it even make sense to invest CapEx into these more structurally challenging buildings?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
I think it's very difficult to answer generally what to do. It has to be case by case. In some cases, it makes sense to upgrade the unit and adapt it to the wishes of the tenant. In other cases, it might be giving a discount. In other cases, it's just answering faster than is done historically. It's very different, and you have to look it on a case by case, on a case by case. What we've said is that we have to be more flexible, we have to be faster, and we have to really listen into what the clients are wishing for, so that we can grab the clients that are out there before our competitors can grab them.
John Vuong
Director of Equity Research, Kempen
Just maybe to ask it differently, do you see the CapEx spend in, say, 2026, 2027 to be higher than 2024, 2025?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
Reluctant to speculate, but I would say it's probably will be around the same level as, as this year.
James Cattell
Associate, Green Street
Okay. That's clear. Thank you.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Thank you. Next question, Paul May, Barclays.
Paul May
Director and Head Real Estate Equity Research, Barclays
Hi, guys. Thanks for the presentations. I got three questions. Two are linked, so I'll ask those together. You've obviously mentioned you're focused on leasing, leasing, leasing. I just wondered what your view is on the rental value per square meter, i.e., are you focused purely on reducing vacancy, in which case you'll allow rent concessions, lower rents to come through? Or are you focused on rent per square meter, in which case you'll happily have a higher vacancy holding out for that higher rent. Just to get a sense there. Then linked to that, can you give us some color on where your current portfolio rental income sits versus market rent? You know, if all your tenants left and you relet all of your assets today, would that be at a higher or lower rent than you've currently got in the portfolio, assuming that there were tenants available for that? I've got another question, but I shall ask in a second. Thanks.
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
Very good questions. If I may answer the second one first. It's a difficult one, but I appreciate the question, and it has to be booked a bit on the speculation side from my side. I would say that we probably would reach roughly the same level as we have today. If every one of our tenants left, we would have some premises that would be rented on a high level, some on a lower level, but on average, roughly about where we are today. The first one, could you repeat that one?
Paul May
Director and Head Real Estate Equity Research, Barclays
Yeah, it's just, it's just looking and thinking how, how you think about leasing. Which is also the focus. You know- Is it just reducing vacancy and therefore you give rent concessions? Or is it we're focused on the rental level-
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
Good point.
Paul May
Director and Head Real Estate Equity Research, Barclays
In which case we live with higher vacancy.
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
It's completely dependent on actually the market and sort of the demand in the market. In some markets, we really have to give concessions, lower the rent to get a tenant, instead of have cash flow and not having cash flow. In other markets, it's better to wait because there, we know that there's demand there, and we write the lease contract over five or seven years, then we don't want to lock in a too low rent level, obviously. Again, boring answer, understand that, but it's really on case by case, depending actually on the particular building we are looking at, not dependent on the particular market or asset class. It's really on case by case. That's one of the things we've really been talking about here since back to basics, that we really need to have a smart thinking about every premises we have within the portfolio.
Paul May
Director and Head Real Estate Equity Research, Barclays
Yeah, I mean, similar to what we're seeing in other markets, but as you say, it's very asset specific, not necessarily market or submarket specific. Just a final one, you mentioned Entra is not hurting, but just looking at their reporting, vacancy has been increasing and its earnings yield is much lower than your earnings yield. You could argue that capital would be better spent selling Entra and basically buying back your shares. You announced, obviously, the share buyback today. I just wondered how you think about that and where the comment around Entra is not hurting us, it's benefiting us, when actually, if you look at the numbers, you could argue the opposite, that it would be better to rotate that capital elsewhere. Thanks.
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
I would agree to some extent to what you're, what you're saying, that we could probably, if we had the cash, use it wisely as well, not just having it in M, in Entra. Entra is also in the market where demand has fallen a bit, compared to as it was before, but not as much perhaps as in Stockholm or Copenhagen. I was tilting more towards, that when I said that the Entra is not hurting us, at least.
Paul May
Director and Head Real Estate Equity Research, Barclays
Okay. The underlying market is a bit better positioned than some of your other markets. Is that-
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
I would say, yes. Yes.
Paul May
Director and Head Real Estate Equity Research, Barclays
Yeah. Okay, perfect. Thank you very much.
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
Thank you.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Thank you. Next question, James from Green Street.
James Cattell
Associate, Green Street
Good morning. You mentioned some one-off costs associated with canceling projects. Would you possibly be able to let me know if the, the number of projects canceled was higher than usual? Maybe what the nature of these projects was, how much CapEx was associated with this, and then maybe how or why you made the decision to cancel these projects.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
I mean, that was early stage ones. That is, of course, something that we are always doing, sort of going through actually every quarter. Then, of course, sometimes you put it more on a spot, not any specific areas or, so more business as usual, a little bit higher than usual.
James Cattell
Associate, Green Street
Okay, thank you.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Thank you. Next question, Fredrik Stensved of ABG Sundal Collier.
Fredrik Stensved
Equity Research Analyst, ABG Sundal Collier
Thank you. Morning. I have two follow-ups on the transaction market comment you made earlier, Pål, where you alluded to a relatively strong market on the sort of back of cheap financing. The first one is, are you able to call out any specific segments in your current portfolio, which might be up for sale and where you believe interest would be high in the market? Secondly, looking at the transaction market and the interest and your decision to do share buybacks today, do you believe it is possible to find the sort of, you know, acquisitions of decent volume or size in the direct market, which are more attractive than your own share at this moment? Thanks.
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
Yeah, thank you. I think the transaction market, as I said, it's driven now by a lot of funding being available to low spreads. That, that's the main, main driver. Also, I think there's been a couple of years where companies have not done that many transactions, and that's also driven up demand a bit. They see the potential now for restructuring their, their portfolios. If there are any specific parts of our portfolio which have extra interest from potential buyers, no, I, I can-- no, I can't really say that at this stage, actually. No, I, I... We have lots of discussions with people, and it's, a broad palette of different types of discussions, I would say. Now I have to ask you to repeat the other questions.
Fredrik Stensved
Equity Research Analyst, ABG Sundal Collier
Yeah, sure. The second one is on the back of your decision to do share buybacks and the current discount, NAV, and the transaction market today, do you believe it is possible to find acquisitions in the direct market, which are more attractive than your own share?
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
Possible, but difficult.
Fredrik Stensved
Equity Research Analyst, ABG Sundal Collier
That's good enough. Thank you.
Pål Ahlsén
CEO, Castellum
Thank you.
Christoffer Strömbäck
Acting CFO, Castellum
Thank you, Fredrik. That was actually the last question for today. Thank you all for listening, and have a great day.
